paragraphs: Rav Mari, son of the daughter of Shmuel bar Shilat.

Bava Batra 61b mentions him. The supplied transcription has him reporting in his father’s name. Hyman reports that the words bar Shilat had already been removed from the Talmudic passage and are also absent in Dikdukei Soferim.

notes.text: The supplied text says “his father,” while the consulted Bava Batra paragraph reads Abaye. The deletion of bar Shilat is Hyman’s reported textual correction; the present source wording remains unchanged.

The saved whole Davidson Bava Batra61b paragraph reads דאביי (Abaye), whereas the frozen source says דאביו (his father). The body retains the supplied father reading and records the alternative, rejecting the earlier categorical transcription-error verdict. Its parentheses around bar Shilat are digital presentation, not evidence of who deleted words or when. Hyman owns the correction-history and Dikdukei Soferim reports; no apparatus was newly inspected or maternal chain changed.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. III, p. 907) and the consulted Bava Batra 61b both read “in Abaye’s name.” The supplied transcription reads “in his father’s name.” Dikdukei Soferim’s printed-text column gives bar Shilat in parentheses, and its manuscript column and note record the omission. Hyman retains bar Shilat in his heading.
